new_findings.message: Reconciliation-log retention bound is qualitative ('max retention') with an overflow alert but no drafted ceiling (entries/bytes/age); the exhaustion path is named but not dimensioned. Acceptable to calibrate at TDD, but the bound should carry a placeholder magnitude so the overflow test is constructable at the boundary.

Circuit-break OPEN is specified for get/claim, but the reclose (half-open probe / reset) semantics are implicit. Under a transient substrate blip the recovery path that re-admits traffic is undefined. Add a reset/half-open contract (TDD may bind the timing).

note: Patch closes all four C1 dimensions CHAOS-002 flagged. (a) Throughput per-operation (get >=500 read/s, claim >=50 write/s, increment_visits >=500/s). (b) Error budgets concrete with an allowed-failure ceiling (get >=99.9% / StoreUnavailableError <=0.1%; claim >=99.9% durable-commit + RPO=0), so 'fail-safe degrade' now has a quantified rate. (c) Measurement methodology stated: server-side observation point, rolling 5-min percentile window, at design load, error budget = StoreUnavailableError/timeout fraction. (d) get latency allocation quantified as <=10 ms p95 (store's slice) with >=40 ms reserved for handler/network within the 50 ms redirect budget, making the component NFR independently testable at the boundary. Beyond the ask, the new Resilience envelope (1.5x overload margin, fail-fast shed, explicit shed order increment->claim->get, bounded CODE_TAKEN retry default 5 with terminal exhaustion, bounded reconciliation log with overflow alert) and the §3 per-boundary timeout/retry/circuit-break table harden accidental-failure paths. Concrete numbers are clearly drafted SPEC allocations for TDD calibration; the contract shape is complete. Residual gaps are non-blocking P3s. No new P0/P1 in the patched region; no regression. lens_score 74 -> 89.
